rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies oxidation behavior of a bulk arc-melted AlCrCoFeNi alloy under heating in air/vacuum, while the hidden target studies room-temperature nanoindentation creep of sputtered Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer coatings with varying modulation periods. These are completely different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses high-temperature heating (up to 1100 °C) in air or vacuum, whereas the hidden target uses room-temperature nanoindentation creep at controlled loading rates. The conditions are entirely different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes selective oxidation via outward Al/Cr diffusion and phase transformations, while the hidden target proposes dislocation-interface interactions leading to interfacial amorphization and diffusion/interface-slip creep. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts oxidation scale thickness and subsurface phase transformation differences, while the hidden target predicts creep resistance and stress exponent trends. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
